citeAs: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen (2023). MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI. arXiv:2311.16502.
creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen (IN.AI Research, University of Waterloo, The Ohio State University, Carnegie Mellon University, University of Victoria, Princeton University)
description: MMMU (Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning) is a benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. It includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines (Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering) across 30 subjects and 183 subfields, comprising 30 highly heterogeneous image types such as charts, diagrams, maps, tables, music sheets, and chemical structures.
name: MMMU
rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 university students (including co-authors) from various disciplines and subjects served as annotators for data collection. For human expert evaluation, 90 college senior students were selected to represent a wide range of experts in the corresponding 30 subjects (3 student experts per subject).
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: A custom web interface developed by Tianyu Zheng for data annotation and verification.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators (over 50 university students specializing in relevant majors) collected multimodal questions from free online resources, quizzes, textbooks, and other study materials. All questions must contain one or more images, be written in English, meet college-level difficulty, and not be ambiguous. Questions were categorized as multiple-choice or open-ended. Annotators filled in fields including question text, answer options, correct answer, image types, question difficulty, and explanation. Data from sources prohibiting copying or redistribution was explicitly avoided. Annotators were advised to select questions without immediately available answers to mitigate data contamination. A secondary review team vetted annotations for quality and guideline adherence, and regular audits of random samples were conducted.
rai:dataBiases: The manual curation process may carry biases. The focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI. Annotators were advised to select questions without immediately available answers to mitigate data contamination concerns from foundation models. Subjects like law and linguistics were excluded because it was difficult to find enough relevant multimodal problems, which may introduce selection bias toward visually-rich disciplines.
rai:dataCollection: Data was collected in three stages. First, 30 subjects from six disciplines were selected based on the principle that visual inputs should be commonly adopted. Second, over 50 university students (including co-authors) specializing in these majors were recruited as annotators to collect multimodal questions from major textbooks, online resources, and lecture materials, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary. Annotators were instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations and to select questions without immediately available answers (e.g., answers in separate documents or at the end of textbooks). This process resulted in a diverse collection of approximately 13K questions.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Multimodal questions collected from college exams, quizzes, textbooks, online resources, and lecture materials across 30 subjects and 6 disciplines. The raw collection comprised approximately 13K questions before quality filtering.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Document analysis, Secondary Data analysis
rai:dataLimitations: MMMU is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI, as there lacks a direct mapping between performance on MMMU and "90th percentile of skilled adults," nor are college exams the only tasks an AGI shall tackle. The manual curation process may carry biases. The focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI. The benchmark combines multiple-choice questions with concise open-ended questions, which may not capture all aspects of expert reasoning.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Two-stage data cleaning was performed: (1) Lexical overlap and source URL similarity were used to identify potential duplicate problems, which were then reviewed by authors to eliminate duplications. (2) Problems were distributed among co-authors for format and typo checking to ensure adherence to a standardized format. In a third stage, authors categorized problems into four difficulty levels (very easy, easy, medium, hard), and approximately 10% of problems classified as very easy were excluded from the benchmark.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset has a live-updating leaderboard available at https://mmmu-benchmark.github.io/#leaderboard. The paper includes a Version Change Log documenting updates from v1 (Nov. 27, 2023) through v4 (June 13, 2024), with additions of new model results and corrections.
rai:dataSocialImpact: MMMU is intended to stimulate the community to build next-generation multimodal foundation models towards expert artificial general intelligence. The paper notes that Expert AGI (Level 3 in the Morris et al. taxonomy) marks a critical milestone denoting AI that reaches "at least 90th percentile of skilled adults" in a broad range of tasks, which could lead to significant risks of job displacement and economic disruption. The authors caution that MMMU is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI but argue strong performance should be a necessary criterion.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating multimodal foundation models on college-level multi-discipline understanding and reasoning tasks; benchmarking progress towards Expert AGI; assessing expert-level visual perception, domain knowledge recall, and deliberate reasoning capabilities of large multimodal models (LMMs).
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The data annotation protocol explicitly states that annotators should avoid collecting questions that contain any private information. The dataset consists of college-level academic questions and does not intentionally include personal or sensitive information.

null_reasons.publisher: No single publishing organization is identified; the dataset is a collaborative effort across multiple universities and research institutions with no single publisher named.
null_reasons.license: No license is explicitly stated in the paper for the dataset itself.
null_reasons.rai:annotationsPerItem: The paper does not specify a fixed number of independent annotations collected per item; questions were collected and reviewed but no per-item annotation count is given.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: No inter-annotator agreement metrics or formal annotation quality analysis statistics are reported in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The paper does not discuss missing data handling in the collection process.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: No specific timeframe (start/end dates) for data collection is mentioned in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation protocol is described; the dataset consists of discrete Q&A items without missing value imputation.
null_reasons.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: No post-collection data manipulation (augmentation, resampling, balancing) is described for the dataset itself.
null_reasons.rai:machineAnnotationTools: No machine learning tools or automated annotation tools were used in the dataset annotation pipeline; annotation was performed manually by human annotators.
